role.altitude: The announcer keeps choosing stories, finding the angle, picking music with producers and talking on air; scanning wires one by one, rewriting copy to length from scratch, writing every aired item into a log and sorting listener messages by hand shrink.
skills_to_grow: Editing drafted scripts for the ear
role.ambitious_version: An announcer who spends the prep time on the angle and the listener, not on logs and lists.

tasks.short: Gather news, sports and weather material, select stories, rewrite material into scripts that fit the time slot, time and rehearse, have the final script checked, and deliver the report on air.

steps.what: Announcer gathers news, sports and weather material from wires and services
Announcer selects the stories for the bulletin
Announcer rewrites the material into scripts that fit the time slot

loop.input: The chosen wire articles and the slot length.
loop.output: Radio scripts written for the ear, with read time.
loop.check: Every fact, name, number and quote must appear in the source article; any extra stops the draft; read time must fit the slot. The announcer reads each script against its article: same meaning, nothing claimed beyond the article, attribution kept; scripts that do not match are rewritten.
loop.stop: The announcer rewrites by hand when a draft fails the check twice.
loop.why_not_simpler: Wire copy is written for reading, not for the ear.

steps.what: Announcer times and rehearses the bulletin
Editor checks and approves the final script
Announcer delivers the news, sports or weather report on air

approvals.approved_version: The bulletin script as approved by the editor in s5; a story changed after approval is read only after the editor checks the change.

tasks.design: A wire dashboard filters agency copy, weather service output and sports results by region and topic, instead of the announcer scanning each feed. Selecting stories stays with the announcer. A drafting step turns the chosen articles into radio scripts with read time, and every fact, name and quote must appear in the source. The announcer edits, times and rehearses; an editor checks the final script, and the announcer reads that version on air under editorial responsibility.
tasks.previous_blocker: Wire copy was scanned and rewritten from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: Wire dashboards and drafting checked against the source article.
tasks.still_hard: Breaking news with no wire copy yet.
tasks.human_edge: Telling bad local news in a way listeners can hear.
tasks.altitude: Less scanning and rewriting; selection and voice stay.

evidence.claim: A Dutch news agency tests turning articles into radio scripts with a university lab.
In a trial with 444 professionals writing press releases, reports and emails, a model cut time by 37%.
A former editor was suspended for AI-invented quotes, so every quote is checked against the source.
The journalists' model guideline asks for a final check by another person.

assumptions: Boundary: preparing and delivering reports; reading news flashes (task 3925) and writing scripts for broadcasts (task 20889) are sibling tasks.
The editor's check in s5 is new labour, shown and excluded from the announcer's hours.
Selecting, rehearsing and delivering keep their full time.
research_questions: Do corrections on air fall with the editor check?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: mostly local news without wire copy (s1 85, s3 90) (5.8); high: many wire-based bulletins (17.2).

tasks.short: Write aired items into the daily program logs, add live elements, check the log against the schedule, and pass it to traffic and rights administration.

steps.what: Announcer writes each aired item, such as musical selections and station promotions, into the daily program log
Announcer adds live elements: live reads, ad-libbed promotions and guests
Announcer checks the log against the schedule and commercial orders
Announcer checks the day's log before release: every flag explained, live entries complete, the right day and station
Announcer passes the log to traffic and rights administration: by mail today, by one release in the playout system after the change

tasks.design: The playout system writes an as-run log of every item it plays, with title, artist and time, instead of the announcer writing each item down. Live reads, ad-libbed promotions and guests are logged with a button in the playout screen. A reconciliation report compares the as-run log with the schedule and commercial orders and flags missing or moved spots for the announcer to explain. Once the announcer has checked the day's log, they release it once in the playout system to traffic and rights administration instead of mailing it.

approvals.approved_version: The day's as-run log with live entries and explained flags exactly as checked by the announcer in s3b, released once in the playout system to traffic and rights administration; any later correction needs a new check.

tasks.previous_blocker: Logs were written by hand and mailed on.
tasks.still_hard: Live events outside the playout system.
tasks.altitude: Most logging goes; explaining exceptions stays.

evidence.claim: Playout logs, revision history and scheduled posts are configuration work.

assumptions: Boundary: program logs; music library organisation (task 20890) is a sibling task.
Input contract for s1: all music, spots and promos run from the playout system, about 80% of aired items; s1 is priced at that share.
s4 saves mailing the log; the release keeps 10. s2 keeps 85: the button records the time, but the announcer still logs each live element.
Logs are used per item aired, not to track the announcer's output.
unknowns: Share of live elements per show.
research_questions: Do log errors in billing fall?

incremental.description: Announcer fixes missing metadata in the playout system.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many live elements and items played outside playout (s1 50, s3 70) (45.3); high: about 80% of items run from playout (64.3).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Scan news, social media and listener messages for topics, develop story lines for broadcasts, research background, and outline them in the rundown.

steps.what: Announcer scans news, social media and listener messages for topics
Announcer develops the angle and story lines for broadcasts
Announcer researches background facts for the story lines
Announcer outlines the story lines in the show rundown

tasks.design: A monitoring dashboard shows trending topics in news and social media and groups listener messages by topic, instead of the announcer scanning each source. Developing the angle and story lines stays with the announcer. The rundown template has fixed fields per item, so the outline is entered once and shared with the producer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sources were scanned one by one.
tasks.still_hard: Local stories that do not trend online.
tasks.human_edge: Finding the angle that makes listeners stay tuned.

evidence.claim: A monitoring tool tracks conversations and news topics.

assumptions: Boundary: developing story lines; studying background information (task 3928) and writing scripts (task 20889) are sibling tasks.
s3 is part of studying background information, which sibling task 3928 covers; its saving is counted there.
Developing the angle keeps its full time.
unknowns: Share of story ideas from online sources.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: mostly local and studio-driven stories, where the dashboard adds little (s1 85) (5.8); high: topic-driven shows (12.0).

tasks.short: Collect listener requests, review audience data, select program content with producers and assistants based on audience tastes and requests, decide the running order, and enter it into the playout schedule.

steps.what: Listener sends a request through the station app
Announcer reviews requests from the public and listener messages
Announcer reviews audience data on listening and music tests
Announcer selects program content in conjunction with producers and assistants
Announcer decides the final running order
Announcer enters the selection into the playout schedule

tasks.design: Listeners send requests through the station app, which groups them by song and topic in one list, instead of the announcer reading mails, texts and call notes separately. An audience dashboard shows listening figures and music test results. Selecting content with producers and deciding the running order stay with the announcer. Music scheduling software builds the hour from rotation rules and the chosen items, and the announcer swaps items instead of entering each one.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests arrived through many channels and playlists were entered item by item.
tasks.enabler_now: Station apps, audience dashboards and music scheduling rules.
tasks.still_hard: Specialist shows with music outside the library.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which request will make the hour.
tasks.altitude: Less sorting and entering; choosing stays.

evidence.claim: Playout logs and scheduling are configuration work in station systems.

assumptions: Boundary: selecting program content; accepting requests on air (task 3935) and the music library (task 20890) are sibling tasks.
Listeners' request time is shown in s1 and is about what a text or call took.
Input contract for s6: rotation rules set by the music director.
Selecting and deciding keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of requests through the app.
research_questions: Does schedule building take less time per show?

incremental.description: Announcer checks the built schedule for clashes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: specialist shows with few requests and hand-picked music (s2 80, s6 80) (13.6); high: format radio with many requests (24.2).
